title: Help with rolling Damage between two specific values

posts.body:
Hi there! Please take the time to read through and follow the template. It has READ in all caps with three exclamations marks for a reason.
READ!!! RPG Maker MZ Support Template
This template will give an idea of what basic support information can help others quickly answer a request.   The more information you provide in the original post, the sooner it can get solved.   A Topical and Meaningful Thread Title  Titles such as “help me” and “it’s broken” are not...
forums.rpgmakerweb.com
For example, you are showing a note tag in your post, so you'll need to tell us what plugins you are using, as well as provide a screenshot of where and how you've implemented this.
Just answering the part about "rolling between two values", you could use Math.randomInt(x) for that, a variation of Math.random() that was added in RPG Maker. The damage would be calculated as:
Math.randomInt(MaxDamage - MinDamage) + MinDamage

posts.author: King Nothing
Canned_Dinosaur
posts.body:
Having a damage of 0 typically means that there is an error in the calculation somewhere (errors in the damage formula are changed to 0 damage). The problem might be that you are using the "this" keyword within the function, but I'm not sure if it's the correct context, as "this" in the damage formula is Game_Action (you can confirm this through console.log(this) in the damage formula).
Secondly, for your hitformula, a b user target are all valid references for the plugin, but "this" will not refer to the user of the skill. You might be able to make it work by changing all instances of "this._hr" to "a._hr", but I'm not too sure actually.
Can do some testing later.
JavaScript:
<hitformula>
a._hr = Math.random()  + (a.hit - b.eva);
a._hr > 0
</hitformula>
EDIT: confirmed that using "this" will neither refer to the user of the skill nor the Game_Action, so that is the cause of your error (and as a result your damage showing up as 0).
I did some testing with the standard "Attack" skill, using a._hr instead of this._hr, and it looks as if it's doing something. Whether it's as you had envisioned, I cannot tell though.
